title: Long-Lead-Time Prediction of Minimum Air Temperature in Strawberry Greenhouses by Integrating Historical Microclimate Observations and Weather Forecasts
content: Advance forecasts of minimum greenhouse air temperature can help growers plan cold protection for winter strawberries. Regional weather forecasts describe future atmospheric conditions but do not directly represent greenhouse microclimates, whereas local observations capture historical conditions but lack future weather information. We developed a dual-branch model to combine these complementary sources. One branch processes the preceding 12 h of observations using convolution, bidirectional long short-term memory, and attention; the other extracts forecast features through cascaded convolutions. Using winter strawberry greenhouse data from Lin’an, China, we evaluated minimum temperature predictions over 1–12 h windows. Adding the forecast branch reduced root meansquare error and mean absolute error by 30.38% and 21.12%, respectively, relative to the historical-only model. After hyperparameter selection using the dung beetle optimizer, the final model achieved a coefficient of determination of 0.922, a root mean square error of 1.512 ◦C, and a mean absolute error of 1.041 ◦C for the 8 h window. In an independent greenhouse used for cross-greenhouse evaluation, the corresponding values were 0.885, 1.812 ◦C, and 1.141 ◦C. Combining regional forecasts with local observations improved minimum temperature prediction and could support cold-protection planning in strawberry greenhouses.
